tools.title: Tools
tools.hint: The model can call these while it answers. Small models may call them poorly or not at all.
tool.calculator.about: Works out arithmetic exactly, instead of the model guessing.
tool.current_time.about: Tells the model today's date and the time, here or in another time zone.
tools.no_answer: The model stopped after its tool calls without answering. Regenerate, or try a larger model.
tools.waiting: Waiting for you to allow it.
tool.run_python.about: Runs Python code the model writes, in a sandbox, and shows it what it printed.
tool.run_javascript.about: Runs JavaScript with Node.js, in a sandbox, and shows the model what it printed.
tool.run_shell.about: Runs shell commands the model writes, in a sandbox, and shows it their output.
sandbox.title: Code sandbox
sandbox.seatbelt: Code runs in macOS's sandbox: no network, and it can only change its own folder.
sandbox.bubblewrap: Code runs in a bubblewrap sandbox: no network, and it can only change its own folder.
sandbox.none: There's no OS sandbox on this computer: code the model runs can use the network and reach your files. Keep it on Ask first.
sandbox.data_off: Python has its standard library only. Add {packages} (about 300 MB).
sandbox.remove_confirm: Remove the data libraries? Python code goes back to the standard library; you can add them again later.
sandbox.no_node: JavaScript needs Node.js; install it to let models run JavaScript.
sandbox.check_about: Temper tries to get out of it, and shows what held.
sandbox.c.no_secrets: Reading key and credential folders (none here to try)

research.title: Research
research.about: Ask a question; the loaded model searches the web, reads the sources and writes a report that cites them.
research.ask: What do you want to find out?
research.how: It plans searches, reads each source and notes what bears on your question, then writes a report from those notes alone.
research.placeholder: For example: Which open-weight models under 10B parameters are best at coding right now, and how do they compare?
research.depth.quick_about: 3 searches, up to 5 sources. A few minutes.
research.depth.standard_about: 4 searches and a follow-up round, up to 8 sources.
research.depth.thorough_about: 5 searches and two follow-up rounds, up to 14 sources. Can take a while.
research.needs_model: Research uses the model loaded for chat. Load one on the Models page first.
research.delete_confirm: Delete this research and its report?
research.review_hint: Untick a source to leave it out, then write the report again from the rest.
kb.title: Knowledge bases
kb.about: Folders of your documents (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Markdown, text and code) that chat models can search with the Knowledge bases tool. Everything stays on this computer.
kb.embedder_hint: Turns passages into vectors so search finds them by meaning. It runs in llama.cpp, apart from chat's model.
kb.needs_llama: Knowledge bases need llama.cpp. Install it from the Models page.
kb.name: Name
kb.delete_confirm: Delete the knowledge base {name}? Your files stay where they are; only the index is removed.
kb.sync_on: Changes in these folders are indexed within a minute. .gitignore rules are honoured.
kb.sync_off: Index changes by hand with the refresh button.
kb.ocr_vision: Scanned PDF pages are read by the vision model loaded for chat.
kb.ocr_tesseract: Scanned PDF pages are read with Tesseract (a vision model loaded for chat reads them better).
kb.ocr_none: Scanned PDF pages are skipped: load a vision model for chat, or install Tesseract, to read them.
kb.urls_hint: One address per line. Web pages are read as text, YouTube videos as their transcript.
kb.add_url: Add a web page or YouTube link

connect.description: Use the model loaded in Temper from coding agents, editors and your own code through OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs.
connect.no_model: No model is loaded. Requests that name a downloaded model load it while loading on demand is on; others fail until you load one on the Models page.
connect.tip: The key stays the same when Temper restarts, so these configs keep working. From a terminal, {start} (or {codex}, {opencode}, {aider}) starts the agent already pointed at the loaded model. Claude Code reads a long system prompt and many tool descriptions, so load the model with a context of 32K or more, and pick one that's good at calling tools.
connect.other_apps_hint: Many apps look for a local model at Ollama's or llama.cpp's usual address. Temper can answer there too, on this computer only. Like Ollama, those addresses take no key.
connect.other_devices_hint: Let phones and other computers on your home network use the loaded model.
connect.linked_hint: Use another computer's models from this one, such as a desktop's GPU from a laptop. On that computer, turn on serving on the network and make an API key, then link it here. Ask for its models as {name}; a model only it has can be asked for by name alone. The preferred device answers for models both computers have.
connect.decisions_hint: Typed answers for your apps: yes or no, one of a set, labels or a score, each with a reason. Save a question by name and an app sends only the text, to {path}. The loaded model answers, or a classifier you trained on the Train page.
connect.api_keys_hint: Give each app or device its own key instead of Temper's, so you can see what each one uses and revoke it on its own. These keys open the model API ({path}) and nothing else.
connect.requests_hint: The latest calls to the model API, including Temper's own chats.
connect.mcp_hint: Agents that speak the Model Context Protocol can use Temper as a server at {url}: list and load this computer's models, ask them questions, and follow or cancel downloads, training and exports. It uses the same key.
connect.mcp_tip: Or, from a terminal: {add} (or {codex}, {cursor}, {vscode}) adds it for you, and {doctor} checks it.
